title: Small polynomial presentation pair categories and canonical base change
statement: Fix an infinite set $I$ as a common size bound [def-weil-size-convention], commutative rings $A,B$ with a ring map $A\to B$, and a subset $E\subseteq I$; put $C=B[E]$. Let $\mathcal D^+$ have objects $(T,\gamma)$ with $T\subseteq I$ and $\gamma:T\to C$, representing the polynomial $B$-algebra $B[T]$ with augmentation given by evaluation at $\gamma$. Its morphisms are augmentation-preserving $B$-algebra maps. Let $\mathcal P^+$ have objects $(S,T,\beta,\gamma)$ with $S,T\subseteq I$, an $A$-algebra map $\beta:A[S]\to B$, and $\gamma:T\to C$; these represent $P=A[S]$, $Q=P[T]$, with compatible augmentations $P\to B$ and $Q\to C$ determined by $\beta,\gamma$. Morphisms are commuting pairs of $A$-algebra maps on $P,Q$ preserving both augmentations. Define $v^+:\mathcal P^+\to\mathcal D^+$ by $(S,T,\beta,\gamma)\mapsto(T,\gamma)$: the algebra is the canonical base change $Q\otimes_P B=B[T]$, and the morphism is the unique $B$-algebra map commuting with coefficient specialization $Q\to B[T]$. The identity-augmented object $C$ of $\mathcal D^+$ is $(E,(e\mapsto X_e))$ and the canonical arrow $(T,\gamma)\to C$ is its evaluation augmentation. The opposite categories and the opposite functor give the presentation sites and their base-change functor.

lean.note: Small coordinate representatives using subsets of the common bound. PairHom stores the induced B-algebra map together with its full specialization square: B-linearity and the square on X determine it uniquely; it exists for every commuting pair by the free-polynomial universal property. The categories therefore contain exactly the source morphisms, with no extra mathematical restriction.
